front: Three DDoS families and their defence layer?
back: Volumetric (anycast scrubbing), protocol such as SYN floods (SYN cookies, load balancers), application L7 (cache, WAF, rate limits, load shedding).
Spoof the victim's address on small UDP requests to open servers; their much larger replies go to the victim. UDP has no handshake to check the source.

front: Why can't you defend a 50 Gbps flood at a 10 Gbps origin?
back: The link is full before packets reach your firewall. The traffic must land on a network with more capacity than the attack.
The server encodes connection details in its sequence number and allocates state only when a valid ACK returns, so spoofed SYNs fill nothing.

front: Why do per-IP limits miss distributed L7 floods?
back: 200,000 rps from 20,000 bots is 10 rps each, which looks normal. Cache, detect bots, and rate-limit per user or key.
Accept origin traffic only from the CDN's ranges or an authenticated tunnel, so attackers can't bypass the CDN by hitting the origin IP.

front: Root cause of every injection bug?
back: Untrusted data mixed with code and sent to an interpreter (SQL, shell, HTML, templates, logging), which can't tell them apart.

front: Why do parameterised queries beat escaping?
back: The SQL is parsed before the value arrives, so the value can only be data. Escaping must get every dialect and context right.

front: What can't be a bound parameter?
back: Identifiers: table and column names, ORDER BY direction. Map input through an allowlist.
Log4j 2 evaluated lookup expressions in logged strings, so a logged header could make the server fetch and run remote code (CVE-2021-44228).
Contextual output encoding by default, sanitise any HTML you must render, Content Security Policy as a backstop, HttpOnly cookies.
An attacker makes your server send requests to destinations they choose, reaching internal services and cloud metadata from inside the trust boundary.

front: How does IMDSv2 stop typical SSRF?
back: Credentials need a token from a PUT with a custom header; the token has a hop limit of 1 by default and requests with X-Forwarded-For are refused.
A name resolves to a public IP when checked and a private one when fetched. Resolve once, validate, connect to that exact IP.
SSRF through a misconfigured WAF, then role credentials from IMDSv1, then a role with broad S3 read access. Any one control would have broken it.
A01 Broken Access Control, A02 Cryptographic Failures, A03 Injection (including XSS).

front: Is the OWASP Top 10 a security standard?
back: No, it is an awareness ranking of risk categories. OWASP ASVS is the verification standard.
